acceptance: A decision: raise the capacity to at least 300 files, or accept the current limit with the reason
A test pins the boundary (largest file count that keeps the map, and the next size up falls back to the digest)
docs/operations/oracle-review-v2.md states the file count above which follow-ups become full reviews
The #2784 description's 300-file claim is corrected, or a correcting comment is posted on #2784
context: Found in the completion audit of the oracle protocol on 2026-10-09. Probe: encode_marker over protocol.patch_map of N synthetic paths benchbox/core/equivalence/file_NNNN.py with sha256 patch hashes.
description:
The hidden `oracle-protocol` marker is capped at 4096 bytes (protocol.MARKER_LIMIT). Above the cap, encode_marker keeps only the aggregate patch digest and drops the per-file patch map. Without the map, changed_paths treats every file as changed, so the next round after SHIP or SHIP WITH FIXES is a full review rather than one scoped to changed files. That fails safe but costs reviewer time and can count defects in files the author never touched.

Measured on develop e7eb5ce7e with a 10-defect record and 200-character titles (the test's shape): the map is kept up to 200 files, and up to 210 with no open defects. The merged #2784 description says "A 300-file marker fits with its patch map; a 1000-file one keeps only the digest", and the handoff asked for a 300-file test; the tests cover only 100 files (map kept) and 1000 files (digest only), so nothing pins the real boundary.

Options: shorten what each entry stores (the 8-hex path hash plus 16-hex patch hash dominate, and random hex compresses poorly), raise the cap if GitHub review bodies allow it, or accept the limit and document it.
